notes: Authentic scene identity and rights survive transformation. Separate venues never become a continuous physical 3D walk.
An object hotspot is not a separate image; all six share the exact original Brompton altar still.
Independent museum/reference photos cannot prove a pictured object is present at Brompton nor a specific 1962 rubric.
Reference illustrations do not count as photographic object coverage; the 1948 image has jurisdictional rights caveats.
No AI-generated imagery, no historical picture substituted as evidence of the actual Mass in that venue.
Do not duplicate or update G###/VMQ/Mass Explorer or LIVE/Simple/Missal owners as part of this registry.

objects.label: Tunicle
objects.difference_from_dalmatic_note: Tunicle/tunicella is closely related to the dalmatic but must be shown as subdeacon's attire or identified museum tunicle, not merely copied from the deacon's dalmatic record.

objects.label: Liturgical vestment colour set
objects.coverage_note: Do not mark complete from single colour, a digital schematic, or improperly conflated modern colour selection. Source separate 1962-valid fabric photographs and present as a controlled five-variant set.

color_set_photo_requirements.limitations: Objects differ in date, style and venue, white example includes red features and violet lacks independently established Roman Catholic venue; these are five research images not proof of one liturgical collection or 1962 ceremonial use.

composite_photo_requirements.licence_and_use_caveat: Three different original venues and eras; do not construct a supposed single historical ensemble; each is independently credited.
